title: Harness integration: customer scripting & throughput strategy

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 16:30 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SRE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Sofia Ruiz, Tom Baxter, Nina Park, Raj Patel, Evan Cole (Brightlane)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be terse): Review of benchmark harness integration, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, success criteria draft, instrumentation points, timeline for POC.

[00:00:08] Lena: Hey everyone, good afternoon — thanks for carving time. Quick intro — I'm Lena, AE on the account, Omar is our SE who will lead the harness integration.
[00:00:20] Sofia: Hi! Sofia here, head of AI at Brightlane. We have Nina and Tom on to talk details. Sorry if we're a bit late, east coast schedule.
[00:00:28] Omar: No problem. Brief agenda — we want to align on the scripts you currently run, what your success criteria are, and whether we'll run streaming or non-streaming loads for the POC. Also call out VPC and security constraints.
[00:00:40] Tom: Sounds good. For context, our current harness is a modified locust-based system that drives a mix of chat and single-turn generative calls. We have about 3 canonical scripts: triage-chat, discharge-summary, and reranker-batch. The chat traffic is more latency-sensitive.
[00:00:55] Marcus: Quick Q — when you say locust, is that pure HTTP non-streaming, or are you doing websocket/streaming for the chat?
[00:01:05] Tom: Right now non-streaming HTTP long polling. But for the product we'd like to evaluate streaming because our UX streams partial tokens to users.
[00:01:13] Nina: Also note token lengths vary wildly — triage-chat often 200-700 tokens, discharge-summary is 1k-2k tokens in the gold set. Our success metric is quality + latency for chat.
[00:01:26] Raj: Security note: anything running against our data has to be in our VPC; we cannot send PHI outside and we need KMS integration.
[00:01:33] Priya: Good to call out. We can support Private deployment or dedicated pools with VPC peering — we'll capture network requirements as action items.
[00:01:40] Evan: Timeline ideally: a one-month POC, with a 48-hour focused benchmark in week 2. Goal is to decide on dedicated vs hosted after results.
[00:01:49] Lena: Ok, let's build a proposal in this call. Can we talk success criteria? What metrics do you need to sign off?
[00:01:56] Sofia: Primary: chat p95 < 250ms for short completions (<200 tokens), p99 < 1s for same. Secondary: throughput — sustained 100-150 reqs/s across mixed profile. Tertiary: cost per 1k tokens target to be within our current budget threshold.
[00:02:12] Omar: That's a tight p95 for short completions — are you assuming streaming helps reduce perceived latency?
[00:02:19] Nina: Yes, for chat perceived latency is more important; streaming will give us earlier token delivery. But for the SLOs we gave above we're measuring server-side time to first token and time-to-complete as separate metrics.
[00:02:30] Marcus: Note: our harness supports measuring time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streaming vs non-streaming; we'll return both. Also can correlate with client-side traces if you add the headers.
[00:02:40] Tom: On workload sizing: peak plan for 150 rps sustained over a 10-minute window, burst to 400 rps for short periods. Average request size ~500 tokens.
[00:02:50] Omar: For throughput planning we need token/sec capacity estimates for the model variant — do you have a preferred model family?
[00:02:57] Sofia: We're experimenting with a 8B open-weights model right now; we might test a quantized 8B and a 16B baseline. We want to see perf delta and quality tradeoffs.
[00:03:07] Lena: Perfect. We'll propose a matrix: quantized-8B (int8), 8B fp16, 16B fp16. For each run we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and token cost.

[00:03:27] -- Topic: Harness integration specifics --
[00:03:30] Omar: Walk me through your current script outputs. Do your scripts assert completions or diff against golden refs?
[00:03:36] Nina: We have a scoring harness — it runs the calls, collects outputs, computes BLEU/ROUGE-ish measures and a few human-simulated labels. For chat there's also a re-ranking step and a safety filter.
[00:03:46] Omar: Ok. Best plan: we adapt your scripts to call the Redwood harness shim which records timestamps at the send, first-token, and end-of-stream. We'll need you to mark which scripts must use streaming.
[00:03:58] Nina: Understood. We'll mark triage-chat as streaming. Discharge-summary can be non-streaming. Reranker-batch is batch, non-streaming.
[00:04:07] Marcus: A few integration gotchas we've seen: 1) some client libs don't handle chunked transfer encoding well, 2) proxies can buffer streams and destroy perceived streaming benefits. We'll need Tom's list of proxy settings.
[00:04:20] Tom: We have an nginx+grpc-proxy in front of our services — I'll paste config snippets.
[00:04:27] Raj: Also make sure logs don't include PHI. We require redaction at the agent boundary.
[00:04:32] Priya: We can support an agent-side redaction hook; we should capture what fields to redact.

[00:04:45] -- Topic: Benchmark plan and telemetry --
[00:04:50] Omar: Proposed plan: Day 0 smoke + integration; Day 1-2 baseline runs at low concurrency; Day 3 reserved 48-hour sustained load window with mid and high concurrency; Day 5 analysis and write-up. Does that align with your timeline?
[00:05:01] Evan: Yes. We want the 48-hour window to include our failover tests (region switch) and a canary config where quantization is toggled.
[00:05:10] Lena: We'll need to reserve dedicated capacity for that 48-hour run to avoid noisy neighbors. Priya — can Redwood reserve a dedicated pool for customer POCs?
[00:05:17] Priya: Yes, we can provision a dedicated pool and pin the model versions; we will bill usage to the POC account. We'll need to set autoscale floor and ceiling for the run.
[00:05:25] Tom: On observability we need token-level cost/latency breakdown. Can the harness emit that?
[00:05:30] Marcus: The harness can emit per-request token counts plus latency buckets. We'll push results to your S3-compatible bucket with a standardized CSV and JSON per-run.
[00:05:39] Nina: Important: please include KV cache hit telemetry — we cache prefixes heavily in production and that affects tokens/sec and latency.
[00:05:46] Omar: We'll surface a 'cache hit' flag per request. Also note that continuous batching behaviors can change perf for short bursts. We'll test with batching disabled and with tuned batch windows.

[00:06:05] -- Topic: Streaming vs Non-streaming tradeoffs --
[00:06:09] Marcus: Streaming reduces time-to-first-token but increases concurrency on the serving side because connections remain open longer. For throughput tests we must account for connection limits.
[00:06:18] Raj: So there's a capacity tradeoff — streaming may require more sockets/ephemeral resources; how do you model that?
[00:06:23] Priya: We run network concurrency stress tests and measure p95 under socket-saturated conditions. Our autoscaler can be tuned but we want to surface the cost delta between streaming and short-polling.
[00:06:33] Nina: For our UX perceived latency matters more — so if streaming costs +15% in hardware but halves p95 perceived, it's worth it.
[00:06:40] Omar: We'll include cost-per-utility metrics in the report, e.g., dollars per % of users meeting the SLO.

[00:06:52] -- Topic: Instrumentation and script edits --
[00:06:55] Lena: Nina, what format are your scripts in? Python? JS?
[00:06:59] Nina: Python, locust-flavored. We also have a small JS harness for the browser side.
[00:07:04] Omar: Great. The integration is a thin shim — a single function to swap your call with our shim and a small decorator to capture headers and timestamps. We'll provide sample patches.
[00:07:13] Nina: One ask: we need to preserve request IDs end-to-end so we can correlate logs.
[00:07:17] Marcus: We'll propagate X-Request-Id. If your scripts set a header we'll capture and pass-through.

[00:07:26] -- Topic: Failure modes and flakiness --
[00:07:30] Omar: Common flakiness - streaming handle lost mid-response, chunked-encoding parsing errors, retries causing duplicates. We'll add idempotency tokens for rerun.
[00:07:40] Tom: Our harness does dedupe by request ID; we'll wire that to Redwood's idempotency key.
[00:07:45] Raj: Also need audit logs for everything — who triggered a benchmark, which scripts ran. Compliance requirement.
[00:07:50] Priya: Audit logs are available in the Private deployment and Dedicated logs can be shipped to your SIEM. We'll make sure run meta is included.

[00:08:02] -- Mid-call calibration: details and clarifications --
[00:08:05] Sofia: Quick check — when you say token cost, are you normalizing across models? We need to compare apples to apples.
[00:08:11] Lena: Yes, we'll compute normalized $/1k input+output tokens and show relative delta by model/quantization.
[00:08:17] Nina: Also want to see quality regressions if any from quantization — can you diff outputs and surface major changes?
[00:08:23] Omar: We will produce a regression table and flag metrics: syntactic drift, hallucination increases measured against your golden set sampling. We'll include human-in-the-loop checks for a subset.

[00:08:37] -- Topic: Network and VPC specifics --
[00:08:40] Tom: For the private tests we will have a NAT/proxy and restrictive egress. Can Redwood's harness run inside our VPC or must we open peering?
[00:08:47] Priya: We can deploy Private control plane connectors and an agent in your VPC. For a POC we can also set up a dedicated endpoints with peering; depends on how tightly you want the control plane.
[00:08:58] Raj: KMS integration is mandatory — keys must be customer-managed.
[00:09:03] Marcus: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM in Private deployments. For dedicated hosted clusters we can integrate with your KMS with limited flow. We'll include a KMS integration matrix.

[00:09:16] -- Topic: Bench specifics — sample run parameters --
[00:09:20] Omar: Proposed sample run matrix (short):
  - Run A: non-streaming, 8B-quantized, steady 100 rps for 30m
  - Run B: streaming, 8B-quantized, steady 100 rps with connection hold, monitor TTFB
  - Run C: non-streaming, 16B-fp16, burst to 400 rps for 10m
  - Run D: caching-enabled vs caching-disabled for triage-chat
[00:09:41] Nina: Can we add a run that simulates slow clients (hold connections open but slow read) to replicate mobile behavior?
[00:09:47] Omar: Yes, we can parameterize client read speed. We'll call that Run E.

[00:09:55] -- Topic: Metrics to collect --
[00:09:58] Marcus: Per-request: request_id, start_ts, first_token_ts, end_ts, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit, model_variant, quantization, error_code. Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, connection count, open sockets.
[00:10:18] Tom: We also want per-customer trace links so SRE can pull traces into our jaeger/tempo stores.
[00:10:23] Priya: We can emit trace IDs in headers; we'll coordinate trace sampling.

[00:10:31] -- Topic: Reporting & deliverables --
[00:10:34] Lena: Deliverables: harness-integration PR, raw run artifacts (CSV/JSON), a short analysis slide deck, a recommendation for model config + cost tradeoff, and a runbook for production rollout. Anything to add?
[00:10:43] Sofia: Include a short section on degraded-mode behavior: if Dedicated pool is exhausted, how does fallback to hosted model work and what are latency implications?
[00:10:52] Omar: We'll simulate fallback paths and quantify the delta in latency and error rates.

[00:11:00] -- Q&A pulse: customer objections --
[00:11:03] Raj: Question — if we run streaming at scale, does Redwood throttle or drop connections? Need behavior defined.
[00:11:09] Priya: We have graceful degradation policies: connection limits, request queueing, and model fallback rings. We'll document thresholds and behaviors.
[00:11:16] Nina: Another blocker — some of our safety filters are third-party and require output inspection. Are you ok with us running that inspection post-response in the harness?
[00:11:24] Marcus: Yes, post-response inspection is fine; just note it affects end-to-end time metrics. We'll capture both pre- and post-inspection timings.

[00:11:36] -- Operational concerns --
[00:11:40] Tom: Billing: how will POC costs be charged? We need a PO or a trial credit approach.
[00:11:45] Lena: For POC we typically offer a combination: credits for initial smoke runs and billable for large dedicated capacity reservation. We'll send pricing and a POC contract addendum.
[00:11:54] Evan: Sales/Procurement will need the SOW and estimate before sign-off.
[00:11:58] Lena: We'll follow up with SOW draft and cost estimate.

[00:12:05] -- Closing operational checklist --
[00:12:09] Omar: Quick checklist: 1) we get scripts + sample dataset, 2) you pick which scripts are streaming, 3) Redwoods share harness patch & smoke run plan, 4) security docs exchange, 5) schedule 48-hour window.
[00:12:20] Nina: We'll upload scripts today and mark streaming flags.
[00:12:24] Tom: I'll send proxy configs and egress rules.
[00:12:28] Sofia: Happy with plan. One more ask: can Redwood also run a cost projection for 6 months if we go production with dedicated?
[00:12:35] Priya: Yes we can provide a capacity-cost forecast given usage profiles.
[00:12:40] Lena: Great. Any other questions?
[00:12:43] Evan: No, that's it. Thanks.
[00:12:46] Lena: I'll recap action items and send notes. Thanks everyone.

[00:12:55] -- End of transcript snippet (automated transcription with occasional mislabels and punctuation issues)

Notes / errors observed: transcription replaced 'KV cache' with 'KV cash' in one line; 'nginx' sometimes shows up as 'engine-x' in the auto text. Speaker labels sometimes collapsed to "Speaker 2" in the raw export; manual attributions added above.
